feedback: Iteration 2 (held geometry, base 1.3, kp 2.4, kd 0.5) is the best race so far at 501.2. The oval completes 20 of 20, and the s-bend completes 6 of 20 with max_error 0.0529 m, under the limit. The slalom still fails: 0 of 20, progress 0.10, max_error 0.063 m, and oscillation of 0.206 on the oval is above the roughly 0.15 level. Line-loss events stay at 0.55 to 1.0 per run, so the ±0.024 m spread is not the limit. Lowering speed did not help the slalom (progress 0.136 at base 1.6 in iteration 1 versus 0.10 at 1.3 in iteration 2), so do not rely on speed alone. The mass reduction you propose is the right kind of lever for oscillation, and I am testing it with the controller held. Hold the iteration-2 geometry for the next race, changing only mass to 0.6 kg, as you propose. Your trigger rules are sound and I will hold you to them. If oval oscillation drops below about 0.15 and slalom max_error reaches or falls below 0.06 m, keep 0.6 kg. If slalom line losses rise above about 2 per run, widen the spread to ±0.032 m. If s-bend completion falls below 0.3, revert toward 0.8 kg rather than adding more spread. Do not change the body, because body width cannot widen the off-track limit at its 0.06 m floor.
requested_changes: Keep the mass at 0.6 kg with all other geometry as in iteration 2 (five sensors at y = 0.06 m, x = ±0.024 m, 12 mm footprint, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.16 by 0.14 m body), so the mass change is the only variable.
If slalom line_loss_events exceed about 2 per run and slalom progress stays below 0.2, widen the sensor spread to x = ±0.032 m with five sensors, keeping y = 0.06 m.
If s-bend completion falls below 0.3 at 0.6 kg, revert mass to 0.8 kg rather than changing the spread, because the s-bend was the track that completed most often under the 0.8 kg design.
